Summary: The official announcement of the Llama 3.1 largest model parameters, 405B, was made on July 23, 2024. The 405B model is part of the Llama 3.1 collection from Meta, which includes models of 8B, 70B, and 405B parameters. This model is available on various platforms including Amazon Bedrock, IBM watsonx.ai, and directly from Meta or Hugging Face. It features a 128K context length, improved reasoning capabilities, and multilingual support in eight languages. The model is also noted for its high performance and scalability, with a maximum prompt and response length of 128,000 tokens.

The Llama 3.1 models are a collection of 8B, 70B, and 405B parameter size models that demonstrate state-of-the-art performance on a wide range of industry benchmarks and offer new capabilities for your generative artificial intelligence (generative AI) applications. [...] All Llama 3.1 models support a 128K context length (an increase of 120K tokens from Llama 3) that has 16 times the capacity of Llama 3 models and improved reasoning for multilingual dialogue use cases in eight languages, including English, German, French, Italian, Portuguese, Hindi, Spanish, and Thai.

You can now use three new Llama 3.1 models from Meta in Amazon Bedrock to build, experiment, and responsibly scale your generative AI ideas: [...] `aws bedrock-runtime invoke-model \

observations.content:
Summary: The largest model of GPT-3, referred to as 175B, contains 175 billion parameters. This model is significantly larger than the previous version, GPT-2, which had 1.5 billion parameters, and also surpasses the largest Transformer-based language model released by Microsoft earlier, which had 17 billion parameters. The 175 billion parameters in GPT-3 are distributed across various components of the model, including input embeddings, transformer blocks, attention heads, and feed-forward layers. The model was trained on V100 GPUs using the cuDNN-accelerated PyTorch framework on a high-bandwidth cluster provided by Microsoft.

Summary: The sources describe GPT-3 as a 175-billion-parameter large language model developed by OpenAI, which was introduced in the paper "Language Models are Few-Shot Learners" in May 2020. It is a decoder-only transformer with 96 layers, a width of 12,288, 96 attention heads of 128 dimensions each, and a context window of 2,048 tokens. The model was trained on 300 billion tokens and has a 50,257-token vocabulary. GPT-3 achieved strong performance on various NLP tasks and can generate news articles that human evaluators find indistinguishable from human-written content. The model was trained using next word prediction, and its sizes range from 125 million to 175 billion parameters.

The largest model has 96 layers, a width of 12,288, 96 attention heads of 128 dimensions each, and a context window of 2,048 tokens, and its layers alternate between dense attention and locally banded sparse attention. It reuses GPT-2's byte-level BPE tokenization with a 50,257-token vocabulary.
